records.real_world_identity_notes: The Corvette C8.R is Chevrolet's mid-engine GTE-class factory race car, built by Pratt & Miller for Corvette Racing on the 2020 Corvette Stingray's aluminum chassis, unveiled in 2019 and competing from 2020 in IMSA GTLM (later GTD Pro) and FIA WEC/Le Mans LMGTE. This PMR observation's telemetry identity ("Corvette C8.R", class GTE) matches the real car directly, and this is the same real car already curated at record_id chevrolet-corvette-c8-r from an existing AMS2 identity. This observation should be added to that existing record as a new PMR simulator identity rather than creating a new record.
records.confidence_basis: Chevrolet's own October 2019 technical reveal (reported firsthand by RACER and Jalopnik, both present at the Road Atlanta presentation) and Wikipedia agree on the manufacturer, model, Pratt & Miller build, competition debut, and Xtrac six-speed sequential transmission architecture, with no conflicting source found for the car's core identity.

records.specification_basis: All three sources independently state a six-speed Xtrac transmission, matching the staged observation and the existing curated record. Two independent firsthand reports of Chevrolet's own technical presentation both describe a sequential racing gearbox replacing the road car's transmission. Neither states whether gear engagement is by dog rings or synchromesh, so this is recorded at the coarser 'sequential' category rather than a specific engagement mechanism, matching the existing curated record's convention. All three sources describe a sequential gearbox, matching the staged observation and the existing curated record. Structural: a throttle blip is a downshift rev-matching technique and is not applicable to upshifts, independent of which car is under review. The reviewed source establishes this is a sequential gearbox to which the concept applies. Structural: an automatic throttle blip is a downshift rev-matching technique and is not applicable to upshifts, independent of which car is under review. The reviewed source establishes this is a sequential gearbox to which the concept applies. Structural: throttle-lift-to-permit-engagement is an upshift concept for a sequential gearbox and is not applicable to downshifts, independent of which car is under review. Structural: an ignition/fuel cut unloads gear teeth under power on an upshift and is not applicable to downshifts, independent of which car is under review. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_actuation, /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shape, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/integrated_display, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/open_top.

records.driver_summary: Xtrac built the C8.R a bespoke P529 six-speed sequential transaxle, unusually compact so the mid-engine car could package it. Paddles, no clutch to pull away, and it cuts and blips for itself.
